skill.name: debug-tauri
skill.description: Debug Tauri WebView apps with process checks, screenshots, log analysis, WebView state capture, and structured reports.
skill.summary: Debug Tauri WebView issues with screenshots, logs, process checks, and reports.
skill.author: 8beeeaaat

security_audit.summary: Most command-execution and hidden-path alerts are documentation examples or expected local helper-script behavior. Confirmed risk centers on screen capture, temp-stored screenshots or logs, a hidden out-of-package reference, and report workflows that can expose sensitive debugging evidence. No prompt injection attempt or network exfiltration was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: Screenshot capture can expose sensitive UI data.
remediation.suggestion: Limit examples to target-window capture, remove or clearly gate primary-monitor and all-window capture, and require user confirmation before any capture.

remediation.issue: Debug screenshots and logs are stored or referenced in shared temp directories.
remediation.suggestion: Use an app-specific private debug directory with restrictive permissions, delete temporary screenshots after validation, and document cleanup steps.

remediation.issue: Generated debug reports can include screenshots, process commands, logs, URLs, and local paths.
remediation.suggestion: Add a redaction checklist before the report template and require removal of tokens, usernames, proprietary UI content, and sensitive URLs before sharing.

remediation.issue: A migration reference points outside the packaged skill into a hidden .claude path.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the out-of-package link or replace it with a packaged, reviewed reference file inside the skill directory.

remediation.issue: Shell helpers execute local process, filesystem, and screenshot commands.
remediation.suggestion: Keep all variables quoted, validate app names and bundle IDs, avoid arbitrary file paths where possible, and show commands before users run them.

semantic_findings.title: Unredacted Debug Evidence Collection
semantic_findings.description: The workflow combines screenshots, process details, console logs, WebView URL, user agent, viewport, and evidence into reports. Without a required redaction step, shared reports can leak sensitive app state, local paths, usernames, tokens, or proprietary UI content.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited workflow and template explicitly ask for screenshots, process status, logs, WebView state, and evidence. I found no mandatory redaction guidance before the data is placed into a shareable report.

semantic_findings.title: Broad Screenshot Scope Beyond Target Window
semantic_findings.description: The screenshot guidance includes capturing all application windows, the primary monitor, and legacy full-screen screenshots. This broad capture scope can collect unrelated desktop content beyond the target Tauri app.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited lines document all-window, monitor, and legacy screen capture paths. The script uses screencapture without limiting capture to a Tauri window.

content.value_statement: Tauri WebView bugs are hard to diagnose when logs, screenshots, and runtime state are scattered. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a repeatable workflow for collecting evidence and writing a clear debug report.
actual_capabilities: Checks whether a named Tauri app process is running.
Captures app screenshots through plugin APIs or legacy macOS commands.
Finds and summarizes Tauri plugin log files across supported platforms.
Collects WebView state details such as URL, title, user agent, and viewport.
Validates debug setup, permissions, plugin logs, screenshots, and project structure.
Guides creation of structured debug reports with evidence and recommended fixes.
limitations: The legacy capture script is macOS-only and requires screen recording permission.
The workflow requires a Tauri app with compatible debug, log, and screenshot plugins.
Screenshots and logs can contain sensitive data and must be reviewed before sharing.
The skill organizes debugging evidence but does not automatically fix application bugs.

use_cases.title: Diagnose WebView Rendering Bugs
use_cases.description: Collect screenshots, logs, and WebView state to understand blank screens, layout failures, or visible runtime errors.

use_cases.title: Validate Debug Tool Setup
use_cases.description: Check whether logging, screenshot capture, permissions, and project structure are ready before reproducing user issues.

use_cases.title: Create Evidence-Based Bug Reports
use_cases.description: Turn process data, console findings, screenshots, and state observations into a structured report for developers.

prompt_templates.title: Check My Tauri App
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner workflow for a running app
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the debug-tauri workflow to check whether my Tauri app is running, capture the current UI state, and summarize the first issues to inspect.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze Logs and Screenshot
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze the latest Tauri screenshot and plugin logs. Identify visible UI problems, recent errors, likely causes, and the next validation steps.

prompt_templates.title: Validate Plugin Migration
prompt_templates.scenario: Migration from legacy scripts to official plugins
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Tauri debug setup against the migration guide. Check logging, screenshots, permissions, file locations, and remaining legacy dependencies.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Debug Report
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced report generation from multiple evidence sources
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a full Tauri debug report from process status, screenshot observations, log statistics, WebView state, root cause analysis, and prioritized fixes.

output_examples.input: A Tauri app opens to a blank window and the developer wants a quick triage.
output: The report states whether the app process is running and records current memory and CPU observations.
It describes the screenshot as a blank WebView and lists visible error indicators if present.
It summarizes recent log errors and recommends checking frontend initialization and WebView permissions first.

output_examples.input: A maintainer is migrating from a macOS screenshot script to official Tauri plugins.
output: The migration review lists old screenshot commands that should be replaced.
It confirms the expected logging and screenshot permissions for the new plugin workflow.
It calls out platform-specific validation tasks for macOS, Windows, and Linux.

output_examples.input: A QA engineer has logs, screenshots, and WebView state from a failed run.
output: The debug report groups evidence by visual state, console logs, WebView metadata, and performance observations.
It separates primary causes from contributing factors and gives concrete next steps for verification.

best_practices: Use official Tauri plugins before legacy platform scripts whenever possible.
Redact screenshots, logs, local paths, URLs, usernames, and command arguments before sharing a report.
Run validation before deep debugging so missing permissions or plugins do not hide the real issue.
anti_patterns: Do not capture the full monitor when an app-window capture is enough.
Do not paste raw logs or screenshots into external systems before reviewing sensitive content.
Do not treat a missing process or missing log file as an application bug without checking setup first.

faq.question: What does this skill help debug?
faq.answer: It helps debug Tauri WebView issues by collecting screenshots, logs, process status, WebView state, and report evidence.

faq.question: Does it require Tauri v2?
faq.answer: The documentation expects Tauri v2 compatible plugins, including tauri-plugin-log and tauri-plugin-screenshots.

faq.question: Can it run on Windows and Linux?
faq.answer: The recommended plugin workflow is cross-platform. The legacy capture script is macOS-only.

faq.question: Does it automatically fix bugs?
faq.answer: No. It collects and organizes evidence so a developer can choose and verify fixes.

faq.question: What data should users protect?
faq.answer: Users should review screenshots, console logs, local file paths, URLs, process commands, and WebView state before sharing.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
